steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Wrap outside of an 8-inch springform pan with aluminum foil, then coat inside with cooking spray.
Spread vanilla wafer crumbs over bottom and up sides of the prepared pan, pressing firmly to adhere.
Beat egg yolks and sugar together in a large bowl. Stir in cream cheese, sour cream, and vanilla extract until smooth; set aside.

Beat egg whites in a separate large glass or metal bowl with an electric mixer until foamy. Add cream of tartar; continue beating until stiff peaks form. Lift your beater or whisk straight up; egg whites should form a sharp peak that holds their shape.

Fold 1/3 egg whites into cream cheese mixture using a rubber spatula or wire whisk. Gently run spatula through center, then around edges of mixture lifting the bottom up and over the center, repeating until fully incorporated. Add the remaining egg whites, folding just until blended. Transfer batter to the prepared pan.

Line a roasting pan with a damp kitchen towel. Place springform pan on towel inside roasting pan; place roasting pan on oven rack. Fill roasting pan with boiling water until reaches halfway up sides of the springform pan.

Bake in the preheated oven until edges nicely puffed and surface is firm except for a small spot in center that jiggles when gently shaken, about 50 minutes. Turn off oven; leave cheesecake in the oven for 1 hour. Cool cheesecake in the refrigerator 4 hours to overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Light and Airy Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: This light and airy cheesecake recipe calls whisks egg whites, combines with cream cheese and minimal sugar for a light, fluffy, and not too sweet cake.
raw_recipe.name: Light and Airy Cheesecake

review.reviewBody: Simple and easy to make. A plain baked cheesecake with a different texture that makes it less filling, less rich than the traditional NY style. I served it with fresh fruit sprinkled with sugar and a mango sauce I made out of mango puree.

I think this recipe makes a fantastic filling, but I'm surprised that there are no instructions for pre-baking the cookie base. I would suggest mixing the wafers with 1/3 cup melted butter and 1/4 sugar in a bow, and then pressing it into the pan. Bake for 10 min at 350°F and set aside to cool before adding the filling.

It is fabulous! I've made it twice. The first time I used chocolate graham cracker crumbs on the bottom & sides, and I added a heaping tsp. of fresh orange zest to the egg-cheese mixture. The second time, I added crushed almond slices to the vanilla wafers on the bottom and sides, included 1 tsp. of almond extract and used a 1/4 cup of Truvia instead of a 1/2 cup of sugar (in fact, it was slightly less than 1/4 cup). Still yummy. I have only one concern: It cracks and "falls" a lot after being taken out of the oven. However, I just re-read the recipe and saw that it was supposed to rest in the oven for an hour after baking. Is that my problem? (Please note I also live at a high altitude. Could this have an impact?) The "falling " is the only reason I gave the recipe 4 stars instead of 5.
I used the recipe but put my own twist on it by adding a chocolate ganache glaze & a 1/4 cup of powdered sugar to the batter. Hands down the best cheesecake I’ve ever had.

This is a pretty flawless recipe. You will not be disappointed. It is exactly as explained "light and airy", which means it is easier to pound back piece after piece :)

Cons: it's a bit of a thin cake, though I think when I use larger eggs and really beat them like crazy it has better results.

Other things: I have tried different crusts, and I prefer ginger snap crust! I have also made this a few times with agave nectar instead of sugar, and it tasted the same(if not better). My favorite is to put cherry pie filling on top, but not much of the sauce, just the actual cherries, and it is SO GOOD!

Simple, light, good. Exactly what I was looking for. I will most likely add butter to the crust next time so it stays together. I did not use the towel, but filled baking pan with water and put under the cheesecake. It worked just fine. My baking time was 40 minutes. I think you really need to watch it after 30 minutes. Thank you for the recipe. I will make it again.

This is a very light, very yummy cheesecake. Very easy to make, too. The vanilla wafer cookie crumbs make a nice, thin, simple crust. I added a few squirts of lemon juice, and subbed part skim ricotta for the sour cream. I'll use this recipe again!

The first time I made this cheesecake my daughter and I made 2. I followed the directions as stated with three exceptions. We didn't let it sit in the oven for an hour and didn't let it chill for 4 hours in the fridge. After it cooled a bit out of the oven we ate it! Then we made the second one and did the same! This is our favorite cheesecake. Great tasting and with simple directions. I did add a tad more vanilla flavoring. Only because I had the dollar store brand on hand. Thank-you for a fantastic recipe!!! XOXOXOXO!!!
This cheesecake is absolutely amazing. I hate dense cheesecakes so this one is perfect and very easy to do

This is just the recipe I've been looking for! I have made this cake 3 times now! My husband was pretty set on NY style cheesecake, until he had this one & loves it over the thick, rich type cake! To compliment it, I slice fresh strawberries or peaches, add splenda to taste and 1tsp granulated sugar to make a thicker juice syrup. (A pint of strawberries sliced thin or 2 large, ripe peaches, peeled & sliced). I mix real heavy whipping cream from scratch to draw the great natural flavors from the cake & fruit! If you haven't tried this recipe, you are missing out!! Note: I was short a half cup of sour cream, so I substituted that 1/2 cup with heavy whipping cream & it was even lighter than b4! I'm baking another cheesecake today & am going to try one full cup of heavy cream, vs. one cup of sour cream. I will let you know results in a few days!! Thank you for sharing this recipe, I make this cheesecake with Graham crust twice per month...we are hooked!! KAL
Very good! Light, not too sweet, and not too rich or filling. I used shortbread cookies for the crust and topped with blackberry purée. Next time will try with chocolate cookie crust and raspberry.
I didn't have sour cream at home, so I used another package of cream cheese. Best cheesecake ever!
Good & Rich. Use parchment paper on pan bottom to avoid sticking
Fluffy Cheese Cake. Wonderful, not too heavy. I added two tablespoons of pancake mix to give it more body.
Brings back memories of the cheesecake my dad use to bring home. This is a good recipe for what I was looking for.
Prefer to the really dense, but I think just a little too soft and fluffy for cheesecake. I think I'll add a little less sour cream next time.
Great light cheesecake. Turned out great!
